title: Office transfers slow while the neighboring test radio operates
scenario: The office AP and a separately authorized test AP use 2.4 GHz, 20 MHz channels. A survey first identifies overlap, then the operator repeats an approved on/off test of the test AP while other conditions remain stable. The excerpts below are an authored diagnostic scenario, not a captured simulator run.

exhibits.title: Radio inventory
exhibits.text:
OFFICE-AP: channel 1, SSID OFFICE
TEST-AP: channel 3, SSID TEST
Client near OFFICE-AP: strong desired signal throughout the test

exhibits.title: Repeated controlled observation
exhibits.text:
TEST-AP transmitting: OFFICE client retries rise sharply; transfer rate falls
TEST-AP radio disabled: retries return near baseline; transfer rate recovers
Repeat trials reproduce the same result; the OFFICE channel remains 1

question: What cause is supported by the combined evidence?
options: A weak desired signal caused by increasing client distance
Interference from overlapping occupied channels 1 and 3
Co-channel contention because the SSIDs have different names
A DFS radar response on the office's 2.4 GHz channel
explanation: The inventory establishes overlap, and the controlled repeatable test supports its effect here. Strong desired signal does not exclude interference; a scan alone would not establish the causal conclusion.
fix: Restore the authorized baseline, then choose an allowed nonoverlapping channel using the complete survey. For a small North American 20 MHz plan, evaluate 1/6/11 across both APs. Change one radio at a time, reconnect clients and repeat the same measurements. Record actual retries and application results; do not infer an optimal channel solely from a neighbor's signal percentage.

title: One client cannot rejoin after the WLAN security change
scenario: STAFF is changed to WPA3-Personal-only. A failing client's OS/driver report and vendor compatibility check confirm that this installed combination supports WPA2-Personal but not SAE. The passphrase is verified unchanged. Other compatible clients connect. The excerpts are representative.

exhibits.title: WLAN settings
exhibits.text:
SSID: STAFF
Band: 5 GHz
Security: WPA3-Personal only
Authentication: SAE
PMF: Required

exhibits.title: Client capability evidence
exhibits.text:
Radio support: 802.11a/n/ac
WPA2-Personal + CCMP: Supported
PMF: Supported
WPA3-Personal / SAE: Not supported by installed OS/driver

question: Which mismatch prevents this client's access?
options: The shared passphrase differs even though it was verified unchanged
The presence of an 802.11ax AP necessarily excludes 802.11ac clients
The client lacks the SAE authentication capability required by this WLAN
The client lacks CCMP even though the capability report lists support
explanation: The security capability evidence establishes the missing SAE support. PMF and CCMP support alone do not make a client WPA3-capable; radio generation names alone do not establish the security method.
fix: Check whether a supported OS/driver update provides the required capability for this hardware. Otherwise replace the client or use a separately approved migration design. On 2.4/5 GHz, a compatible WPA2/WPA3 transition design can allow older WPA2 clients, but they still use WPA2 and do not acquire SAE's properties. Confirm the exact controller security/PMF settings and client compatibility, document the exception, and retest. Do not apply a WPA2 fallback to a 6 GHz-only WLAN.
